title: Nama Group Ediacaran–Cambrian boundary succession, Namibia
summary: The Nama Group of southern Namibia is a well-dated sedimentary record of the final Ediacaran, with volcanic ash beds that give uranium-lead ages around 540–538 million years. The first Treptichnus pedum burrows, a Cambrian marker, appear in its Fish River Subgroup. Its ash-bed ages have been used to place the Ediacaran–Cambrian boundary, but that placement is still debated.

uncertainty.note: Range spans dated Spitskop and Nomtsas ash beds (about 540–538 Ma) to the youngest Swartkloofberg ash bed (537.64 Ma). Ash-bed ages individually carry ±0.1–0.7 Ma; Bowyer et al. 2025 warn some may be over 1 Myr too old.

as_recorded.value: boundary proposed at 538.8–538.6 Ma (Linnemann et al. 2019)
538.58 ± 0.19 Ma, lower Nomtsas Formation ash bed

where.modern_name: Swartkloofberg type area, Witputs Subbasin, southern Namibia
where.historical_name: No polity; Ediacaran foreland basin on the Kalahari Craton

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: PALEOMAP gives 41.10 S, 152.41 W for the same point (a large longitude difference from MERDITH2021); MULLER2019 does not cover 539 Ma. The spread reflects differing reference frames.

importance.justification: The Nama Group supplies radiometric dates and trace fossils bearing on the age and position of the Ediacaran–Cambrian boundary, the base of the animal-rich Phanerozoic.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the boundary: Nelson et al. suggest the Cambrian base may be younger than 537.6 Ma and Bowyer et al. question some ash-bed ages. The pin is the Swartkloofberg area, one of several Nama localities.
